\begin{minipage}{\textwidth}\footnotesize
Verdict words are the registered ones: excluded, not excluded, suitable against dissolution, open (not falsified, no lower bound) and undetermined (data missing). A dash means the test is not applied to the row; route criteria means the row is cell-stage and the route criteria replace $K_2$.\par
\nacreExcludedMark{} \NumExcludedNote. Kinetic stabilisation is not ruled out for phosphates: tier-two class B records exist in \ce{LiPF6} electrolytes, not in fluorine-free ones.\par
Suitable against dissolution is a necessary condition, stated for the cells of the registered grid that pass; it does not address the instability of aluminium above its passivation window and is not evidence of protection. Pass counts are given per row.\par
Acid-adjusted column: split by pH (alternative b): excluded below the lowest pH of the grid that has a passing cell, suitable against dissolution from there up. Slurry-stage $K_1$ is the phase's own ceiling and is not a gate for that stage.\par
\textsuperscript{b}~No $K_{\mathrm{sp}}$ key existed for this phase at the freeze; keys added afterwards are not used in the frozen production.\par
\end{minipage}
